options.content: **Blue = send, orange = receive. Solid = average, dashed = observed peak. Gaps = data unavailable.**

panels.title: RDMA traffic
panels.description: Solid line: average traffic in each time bin. Dashed line: the highest single observation in the bin (a counter read ~2 ms apart), so short spikes stay visible when zoomed out; a single observation has timing jitter and can slightly exceed the link rate. Drag across the chart to zoom in. Gaps: no valid observation (never drawn as 0). Data marked 'live' comes from ainic-netmon record --push: an online approximation; where a push failed the average of that time bin may be off. Import the recording (ainic-netmon-import --replace) for the exact numbers.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: All port traffic (incl. non-RDMA)
panels.description: All traffic through the port, including non-RDMA Ethernet. With firmware IPC: solid line = average per time bin, dashed line = highest observation in the bin (counters read ~2 ms apart). Without firmware IPC (e.g. a VM with a VF): only the lines marked '≈5 s, ethtool', points that each average about 5 s (the firmware updates these counters about every 5 s; zoomed in they are sparse points). ethtool gives a point only when the counters changed: no point means no observed change, not a measured zero. Gaps: no valid observation (never drawn as 0). Data marked 'live' comes from ainic-netmon record --push: an online approximation; where a push failed the average of that time bin may be off. Import the recording (ainic-netmon-import --replace) for the exact numbers.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Retransmitted packets
panels.description: Highest rate per time bin. 0 = observed zero; gaps = no observation.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Congestion notifications
panels.description: Highest rate per time bin. All zero does not prove the network had no pressure: a fabric without ECN marking recovers by drops and retransmission.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: ACK timeouts
panels.description: Highest rate per time bin, per second.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Individual observations (at 1 ms bins each point is one observation; otherwise the highest per $__interval)
panels.description: RDMA traffic as individual observations. Zoom in until the bin is 1 ms to see every observation.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: PFC pause counters (experimental: meaning not yet validated)
PFC pause counters, highest rate per time bin
panels.description: Firmware port counters whose meaning has not been validated yet. Only counters that changed during the recording are imported (ethtool: always). On hosts without firmware IPC (e.g. a VM with a VF) the port statistics come from ethtool instead (lines marked '≈5 s, ethtool'): the firmware updates them about every 5 s, so each point is an average over about 5 s (zoomed in: sparse points). ethtool gives a point only when the counters changed: no point means no observed change, not a measured zero.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

panels.title: Offline report summary (fixed experiment window; does not change with zoom)
panels.description: The offline report's numbers for the experiment's common recording window (ainic-netmon-report shows the window). p99 and the time above 80 % use fine-grained observations only; the average includes long observations.

panels.title: Recording diagnostics (for troubleshooting the monitor itself)
Time without a valid observation (each point: one gap, its length)
panels.description: Collector quality, not network loss: times when a counter could not be turned into a rate (a counter went back, an IPC read was rejected, or the wall-clock position was uncertain). These times are the gaps in the traffic charts. Gaps of different counters are not added up.

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range

properties.value: RDMA counters: counter reset or rejected reading
Port counters: counter reset or rejected reading

panels.title: Recording quality
panels.description: Samples: counter reads saved. Missed sampling slots: sampling times skipped because a read was late (e.g. a firmware stall). Samples lost before saving: the writer could not keep up. Read errors: failed reads.
